text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers refactor to make code easier to read and understand. For example, they may rename variables, split long functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate code. The behavior of the program stays exactly the same, so users do not notice any difference. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor solutions are used. Although refactoring takes time, it makes future changes safer and faster, and it keeps the codebase healthy and easier for the whole team to work with.
